stories.headline: The AI Race Built Faster Chips, Now They're Too Fast for Their Own Wires
stories.summary: As the AI race accelerates, chip speeds have outpaced the capabilities of traditional wiring, creating a critical bottleneck. Eliyan, a Santa Clara startup valued at $1 billion, has secured $145 million in Series C funding to address this hardware limitation.
stories.original_title: The AI race built faster chips. Now the chips are too fast for their own wires.
stories.why_it_matters: AI computers are getting so smart that the wires connecting their parts can’t keep up with the speed of data. This creates a traffic jam that slows everything down, stopping progress unless new, faster wiring is invented. Fixing this is key to making AI actually useful in the real world.
stories.other_side: Some experts argue that building faster chips isn't the only solution. They suggest we should focus on making AI software more efficient instead of just throwing more expensive hardware at the problem.

stories.headline: Why Mainframes Remain Central to Enterprise Transformation
stories.summary: Contrary to predictions of obsolescence, mainframes are being redefined by AI, hybrid cloud integration, and cyber resilience rather than replaced. These legacy systems continue to serve as foundational infrastructure for modern enterprise digital transformation strategies.
stories.original_title: Why mainframes remain central to enterprise transformation
stories.why_it_matters: Old-school mainframe computers are not dying; they are being updated to handle modern AI tasks. This means companies don’t need to scrap their old systems, saving money and reducing waste while staying secure. It proves that legacy tech can still be vital for big businesses.
stories.other_side: Critics say these old machines are heavy, hard to fix, and use too much power. They believe companies should move everything to the cloud for better flexibility and lower long-term costs.

stories.headline: Lloyds Bank Cuts £2bn in Costs via AI-Powered Strategy
stories.summary: Lloyds Banking Group announced a four-year plan to cut £2 billion in costs, driven by an AI-powered strategy aimed at increasing operational efficiency. While the CEO highlighted efficiency gains, specific details regarding potential job losses were not disclosed.
stories.original_title: Lloyds Bank to cut £2bn in costs as part of AI-powered strategy
stories.why_it_matters: A major bank is using AI to cut costs by billions, showing how automation is changing finance. This likely means fewer human workers will be needed for routine tasks in the future. It signals a shift where efficiency matters more than headcount.
stories.other_side: Workers worry that this efficiency drive will lead to mass layoffs without warning. They also fear that relying on AI might make customer service feel cold and impersonal.

stories.headline: Hackers Exploit AnySign4PC to Install Backdoors Without Prompts
stories.summary: A state-sponsored campaign compromised trusted South Korean websites to exploit locally installed financial-security software. Attackers successfully installed backdoors on targeted visitors' systems without triggering standard security prompts.
stories.original_title: Hackers Exploit AnySign4PC via Hacked Korean Sites to Install Backdoors Without Prompts
stories.why_it_matters: Hackers are finding sneaky ways to break into computers without users even knowing it. This makes personal and financial data much more vulnerable to theft. It shows that traditional security warnings are no longer enough to keep people safe.
stories.other_side: Some security firms argue that most users are already protected by basic antivirus software. They claim that blaming complex hacks distracts from the real issue: poor password habits by regular people.

stories.headline: SilverFox Targets Japanese Manufacturer with New BYOVD Chain
stories.summary: The Chinese cybercrime group Silver Fox has been observed executing Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks against a Japanese industrial manufacturer. The campaign utilized new drivers to deliver ValleyRAT malware, highlighting evolving threat vectors in industrial sectors.
stories.original_title: SilverFox Targets Japanese Manufacturer with 3-Driver BYOVD Chain and ValleyRAT
stories.why_it_matters: Cybercriminals are targeting factories and manufacturers, not just banks or stores. This puts physical goods and supply chains at risk of disruption or sabotage. It highlights how digital attacks can now cause real-world damage to industry.
stories.other_side: Industry leaders say that industrial systems are air-gapped and safe from the internet. They argue that these reports exaggerate the threat to scare companies into buying unnecessary security upgrades.

stories.headline: iOS 27 Finally Lets You Hide the Audio Button in Messages
stories.summary: Apple's upcoming iOS 27 update introduces a new customization option allowing users to hide the microphone button in the Messages app. This feature addresses long-standing user complaints about the persistent dictation and audio recording controls cluttering the text entry line.
stories.original_title: iOS 27 finally lets you hide the Audio button in Messages—here’s how
stories.why_it_matters: Apple is finally listening to users who hate cluttered phone screens. Giving people control over what buttons they see improves the daily experience for millions. It sets a trend for other apps to offer more customization options.
stories.other_side: Privacy advocates worry that hiding audio buttons might make it harder to detect when recording is happening. They fear this could be used to spy on people without their knowledge.

stories.headline: Digital PR for AI Visibility: 5 Tactics to Measure Success
stories.summary: With generative AI increasingly shaping search results, having a website is no longer sufficient for visibility. Experts outline five digital PR tactics designed to ensure content is cited and referenced by AI models, along with methods to measure this growing metric.
stories.original_title: Digital PR for AI visibility: 5 tactics + how to measure
stories.why_it_matters: AI search engines are changing how people find information online. Businesses must now write content specifically to be picked up by AI, not just humans. This shifts the entire strategy of online marketing and visibility.
stories.other_side: Critics say this will flood the internet with low-quality, AI-generated spam. They worry that genuine human voices and diverse opinions will get buried under robotic content.

stories.headline: Gpiozero Flow Simplifies Raspberry Pi GPIO Programming
stories.summary: Gpiozero Flow builds upon the Python library originally created in 2015 to simplify programming GPIO devices on Raspberry Pi. By abstracting complex electrical concepts like pin channels and voltages, it allows developers to focus on logical interactions like button presses.
stories.why_it_matters: New tools are making it easier for beginners to build hardware projects with simple code. This lowers the barrier to entry for learning electronics and engineering. It encourages more students and hobbyists to tinker with technology.
stories.other_side: Some developers argue that simplifying the code hides important technical details. They believe beginners need to understand the underlying hardware to truly master programming.

stories.headline: FIFA Forward Enterprise Proposes Tokenized Equity for Private Investors
stories.summary: FIFA is exploring the sale of minority stakes in its commercial arm through tokenized equity, aiming to democratize investment opportunities. This move introduces blockchain-based financial instruments to traditional sports governance, though it raises questions about prioritizing profits over member interests.
stories.original_title: FIFA Forward Enterprise proposes minority stake for private investors, with tokenized equity on the table
stories.why_it_matters: FIFA is using blockchain to let regular people invest in sports organizations. This could bring in huge amounts of cash but changes how sports are governed. It raises questions about whether profit should come before fair play.
stories.other_side: Fans and critics argue that selling off parts of a sports body corrupts its mission. They believe sports should remain independent and focused on competition, not stock market gains.

stories.headline: Secret CLARITY Proposal to Protect Crypto Coders Ripped Apart
stories.summary: A last-minute proposal within the Senate's CLARITY Act negotiations aimed at protecting cryptocurrency developers has faced intense criticism from both political sides. The dispute highlights ongoing tensions in Washington regarding regulatory frameworks for the crypto industry.
stories.original_title: A secret 11th-hour CLARITY proposal to protect crypto coders was just ripped apart by both sides of Washington
stories.why_it_matters: Lawmakers are struggling to create rules for cryptocurrency without hurting innovation. The debate shows how hard it is to regulate fast-moving tech within slow government processes. Poor laws could either stifle growth or allow fraud to thrive.
stories.other_side: Some politicians argue that strict regulations are necessary to protect everyday investors from scams. They claim that without clear rules, crypto remains a wild west dangerous for the public.
